simple.meaning: זִכְרוֹן (zikrôwn) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a memento (or memorable thing, day or writing).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 12:14. The surrounding context includes Torah, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זִכְרוֹן (H2146) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: זִכְרוֹן (zikrôwn) / H2146 is traced through Exodus 12:14, Exodus 13:9, Exodus 17:14, Exodus 28:12 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall keep it as a feast to Yahweh. You shall keep it as a feast throughout your generations by an ordinance forever.
It shall be for a sign to you on your hand, and for a memorial between your eyes, that Yahweh’s law may be in your mouth; for with a strong hand Yahweh has brought you out of Egypt.
Yahweh said to Moses, “Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: that I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky.”
You shall put the two stones on the shoulder straps of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel. Aaron shall bear their names before Yahweh on his two shoulders for a memorial.

You shall take the atonement money from the children of Israel, and shall appoint it for the service of the Tent of Meeting; that it may be a memorial for the children of Israel before Yahweh, to make atonement for your souls.”
He put them on the shoulder straps of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel, as Yahweh commanded Moses.
“Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, there shall be a solemn rest for you, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation.

then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and shall bring her offering for her: one tenth of an ephah* 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel of barley meal. He shall pour no oil on it, nor put frankincense on it, for it is a meal offering of jealousy, a meal offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to memory.

The priest shall set the woman before Yahweh, and let the hair of the woman’s head go loose, and put the meal offering of memorial in her hands, which is the meal offering of jealousy. The priest shall have in his hand the water of bitterness that brings a curse.

“Also in the day of your gladness, and in your set feasts, and in the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be to you for a memorial before your God. I am Yahweh your God.”
It shall happen that the rod of the man whom I shall choose shall bud. I will make the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against you, cease from me.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold of the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and brought it into the Tent of Meeting for a memorial for the children of Israel before Yahweh.

then you shall tell them, ‘Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of Yahweh’s covenant. When it crossed over the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones shall be for a memorial to the children of Israel forever.’ ”
Then I answered them, and said to them, “The God of heaven will prosper us. Therefore we, his servants, will arise and build; but you have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.”
On that night, the king couldn’t sleep. He commanded the book of records of the chronicles to be brought, and they were read to the king.

definitions.short: a memento (or memorable thing, day or writing)
definitions.full: H2146. zikkaron זִכָּרֹן זִכָּרוֺן, noun masculine Eccl 1:11 memorial, remembrance (compare Lg BN 199, 200 ) — absolute זִכָּרוֺן Josh 4:7 +; זִכָּרֹן Exod 28:12 (twice in verse); 28:29 ; construct זִכְרוֺן Eccl 1:11 2 t.; suffix זִכְרוֺנֵךְ Isa 57:8 ; plural הַזִּכְרֹנוֺת Est 6:1 ; suffix זִכְרֹנֵיכֶם Job 13:12 ; — 1 memorial, reminder: a. memorial-day Exod 12:14 (P). b. memorial-usage Exod 13:9 (JE). c. memorial-objects, altar-plates Num 17:5 (P); stones in Jordan Josh 4:7 (JE); crowns in temple Zech 6:14 ; ׳ז in Isa 57:8 is symbol of strange god (Di), or perhaps phallus-image, as sign of harlot (Che), compare > Du (who proposes זְכָרוֺן , from זָכָר ). d. memorial-record ; in a book Exod 17:14 (E); compare זִכָּרוֺן סֵפֶר Mal 3:16 , ׳ס הימים דברי הַזִּכְרֹנות Est 6:1 ; memorial, as proof of citizenship Neh 2:20 (|| צְדָקָה חֵלֶק, ); reminder of Israel, י ׳לִפְנֵי , of הַכִּמֻּרִים כֶּסֶף Exod 30:16 ; spoils of war Num 31:54 ; inscribed stones of ephod Exod 28:12 , 29 , called ז ׳אַבְנֵי 28:12 = 39:7 ; blowing of trumpets Num 10:10 (foregoing all P), compare תְּרוּעַה זִכְרוֺן Lev 23:24 (H; where, however, no י ׳לפני , see Di); (ה)זכרון מִנְחַת Num 5:15 , 18 (P); memorial-sentence, apophthegm Job 13:12 . ** אֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵיֿ זִכְרֹנֵיכֶם 13:12 your memorial words are ashen sayings (i.e. worthless), compare Bu Du; Margolis (privately) suggests that ᵐ5 seems to have read לְאֵפֶר יִמָּשֵׁל [? < רָנְּכֶם ] רָנְיְכֶם your exultation shall be like ashes. 2 remembrance Eccl 1:11 (construct before preposition Ges § 130 , 1), 1:11 ; 2:16 .
